I can see the advantages in a world where war essentially comes down to a contest between machines, and ends when one side runs out of robots. If robots are significantly more effective than human fighters, this may be the result: war becomes a bloodless industrial/design contest played out between emotionless, hyper-aware machines that don't get jumpy and fire on civilians.

The other advantage is: higher-tech weapons are only available to really high-tech societies, and free democracies have huge advantages in technical development. The more high-tech the warfare, then, the greater the natural advantage of free democracies, and the less chance tyrants have of beating us. e.g. Just imagine being able to push a button and deploy ten thousand killer robots to efficiently tear apart Islamic State's forces all across Iraq. Or in a war against China: We can lose because they have many more people, but if it's a contest of pure technology they have no chance.

The third advantage: Technology has more than one use. Any effort put into perfecting military robots would yield knowledge that could be applied to civilian robots as well: autocars, automatic delivery drones, robot police or firefighters or EMTs or doctors or senior care professionals. After all, the only reason we went to the moon was essentially as part of an arms race. Without the World Wars and the Cold War we might barely be exiting the biplane era right now. By putting the lever of success clearly on technical advances (instead of on volume of bodies or courage or metal), we shift resources to where they'll ultimately produce knowledge that benefits humanity the most.
